title: A finite-type monomorphism into an affine-transition limit is eventually monic
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Work with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], with sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. A space is quasi-compact if it admits a surjective etale atlas from a quasi-compact scheme; it is quasi-separated if its absolute diagonal over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is quasi-compact. A morphism is quasi-compact if its pullback along every affine scheme test has quasi-compact source, and quasi-separated if its relative diagonal is quasi-compact. Local finite type and local finite presentation are tested on compatible etale scheme charts [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Finite type means quasi-compact and locally of finite type; finite presentation means quasi-compact, quasi-separated and locally of finite presentation. Let $B$ be an algebraic space, let $I$ be a small nonempty directed set, and let $(Z_i)_{i\in I}$ be an inverse system of algebraic spaces over $B$, with affine transition morphisms (representable by schemes and affine on affine scheme tests). Suppose each $Z_i$ is quasi-separated and $Z=\varprojlim_i Z_i$ exists in algebraic spaces over $B$. Let $A$ be a quasi-compact algebraic space and let $u:A\to Z$ be a $B$-morphism such that $A\to B$ is locally of finite type. If $u$ is a monomorphism, meaning that $A(T)\to Z(T)$ is injective for every $S$-scheme $T$, then there is $i_0\in I$ such that $A\to Z_i$ is a monomorphism for every $i\geq i_0$.

proof.text: Choose an index $0\in I$ and restrict to $i\geq0$. Put $f_i:A\to Z_i$ and $R_i=A\times_{Z_i}A$, with diagonal $\delta_i:A\to R_i$. These fibre products exist by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. The composite $A\to Z_0\to B$ is locally of finite type, so [lem-sfb-space-lft-cancellation] makes $f_0$ locally of finite type. Therefore [lem-sfb-space-lft-diagonal-lfp] makes $\delta_0:A\to R_0$ locally of finite presentation. This uses neither quasi-separatedness of $A$ nor any finiteness property of $Z_0\to B$.

proof.text: Each $R_i$ is quasi-compact. First [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image] identifies the atlas and point-space conventions for quasi-compactness. Since $A$ is quasi-compact and $Z_i$ is quasi-separated, [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-permanence] makes $f_i$ quasi-compact. Base change in [lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-affine-tests] makes $p_2:R_i\to A$ quasi-compact. Choose a quasi-compact scheme atlas $U\to A$. The same test theorem gives quasi-compactness of $E=R_i\times_AU$; choose a quasi-compact scheme atlas $V\to E$. The map $E\to R_i$ is representable surjective etale by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. For every scheme $T\to R_i$, the two scheme maps $T\times_{R_i}V\to T\times_{R_i}E\to T$ are surjective etale, so [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-composition] makes their composite surjective etale. Thus $V\to R_i$ is a quasi-compact scheme atlas. Only the first clause of the permanence node is used; $A$ need not be quasi-separated.

proof.text: For $j\geq i\geq0$, let $q:Z_j\to Z_i$ be the transition. It is affine, hence its diagonal $\Delta_q:Z_j\to Z_j\times_{Z_i}Z_j$ is a representable closed immersion by [lem-sfb-space-affine-locality]. The comparison $R_j\to R_i$ is its pullback along $(f_jp_1,f_jp_2):R_i\to Z_j\times_{Z_i}Z_j$: on a scheme test, a section of this pullback is $(a,b,z)$ with $f_j(a)=z=f_j(b)$, and eliminating $z$ gives $R_j$. On every scheme $T\to R_i$ the resulting projection is precisely the scheme test of $\Delta_q$ along $T\to Z_j\times_{Z_i}Z_j$, hence is a closed immersion. Thus $R_j\to R_i$ is a closed immersion by the definition. In particular $R_i\to R_0$ is closed (the identity when $i=0$).

source.place: Tag 03KN (lemma-fibre-product-after-map), part (3), explicit pullback-of-diagonal argument used in Tag 0828(4)

proof.text: The cone $(\delta_i:A\to R_i)_{i\geq0}$ is a limit cone, also over $R_0$. Indeed, for any algebraic space $T$, a compatible family $T\to R_i$ gives pairs $(a_i,b_i):T\rightrightarrows A$. Transitions preserve both coordinates, and directedness implies $a_i=a_j=a$ and $b_i=b_j=b$ for all $i,j$. The relations say $f_i a=f_i b$ on the tail. For every earlier index $k$, choose $j\geq k,0$ and compose its equality with $Z_j\to Z_k$. Thus all projections of $ua$ and $ub$ to $Z_k$ agree; the given limit property of $Z$ makes $ua=ub$. The common composites to $B$ let us use that limit in spaces over $B$. On every scheme section of $T$, monicity of $u$ gives equality of $a$ and $b$; hence $a=b$ as natural transformations of sheaves. Conversely any $a:T\to A$ gives the compatible diagonal pairs $(a,a)$, uniquely. These constructions are inverse and natural in $T$, proving the limit assertion; the structure map to $R_0$ is $\delta_0$.

source.place: Tag 0828, proof of (4): limit of the kernel pairs equals A, with the cone and cofinal-tail argument written out

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-space-closed-subspace-proper], every closed immersion $R_i\to R_0$ is locally of finite type. Apply [lem-sfb-space-closed-limit-stabilization] with base $B=R_0$, system $(R_i)_{i\geq0}$ and limit $A$: Step 2 supplies quasi-compactness, Step 3 closed transitions, Step 4 the limit identification, and Step 1 local finite presentation of $A\to R_0$. Hence $\delta_{i_0}:A\to A\times_{Z_{i_0}}A$ is an isomorphism for some $i_0\geq0$. If two sections $a,b\in A(T)$ have equal image in $Z_{i_0}(T)$, they define a section of this fibre product. Its unique preimage under $\delta_{i_0}$ has both coordinates equal, so $a=b$. Thus $f_{i_0}$ is monic. For $i\geq i_0$, equality after $f_i$ implies equality after $f_{i_0}$ by composing with $Z_i\to Z_{i_0}$, so $f_i$ is monic as well.
